tavily.text:
To install the Elevation Python package, use the command `pip install elevation`. Ensure that GDAL command line tools, including `gdal_translate`, `gdalbuildvrt`, `gdalinfo`, and `ogrinfo`, are installed and working. For installation details of GDAL command line tools, refer to the GDAL install documentation. Note that Elevation version 2.0 requires Python 3.11 or later.
To install the elevation Python package, use the command `pip install elevation`. Ensure that GDAL command line tools are installed and working. For Windows users, the command `mkdir -p` may not work; instead, use `mkdir`. Note that elevation v2.0 requires Python 3.11 or later. The sources do not provide information on the 'reference' option in the Python API or the specific issue of 'mkdir -p' on Windows being replaced by 'mkdir'.
To install the elevation Python package, you can download the latest version from PyPI. The best way to install it is via pip: `pip install elevation`. Note that starting from version 1.1, only Python 3 is officially supported. For Python 2 support, use `pip install elevation==1.0.6`. Additionally, GDAL command line tools are required, and their installation method varies across operating systems. For GDAL installation details, refer to the GDAL documentation.
